page: Amazon Web Services r5n.24xlarge is a memory-optimized and network-enhanced server type based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor system. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz, delivering 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The instance features a 1:8 core-to-memory ratio, packaging 768.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz (8.0 GB per vCPU). The CPU architecture incorporates 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and support for AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI vector instruction sets. It lacks dedicated local storage and GPUs, depending entirely on network-attached EBS volumes for persistence while providing a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant multi-core throughput alongside high memory and network bandwidth. The instance achieves a top-tier stress-ng multi-core result of 81,307.18 and a PassMark CPU score of 55,814.83, supported by strong encryption and extended instruction metrics. Read memory bandwidth reaches 4,505.69 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 220.43 GB/sec for large 256 MB blocks, complementing strong static web serving throughput (45.88 GB/sec) and high Redis throughput measuring 73.84 million SET operations per second. However, single-core CPU metrics fall into the bottom 25% on stress-ng (1,386.4) and average on Geekbench (1,251.0), and single-threaded gzip compression performs modestly at 23.21 GB/sec.

Hardware tradeoffs center around high network throughput and dense system memory balanced against modest per-thread compute performance and CPU-based inference limitations. Without local NVMe storage or discrete accelerators, workloads relying on ultra-low latency physical disk operations or hardware-accelerated machine learning will encounter bottlenecks; LLM text generation rates consistently rate poor across tested models (e.g., 5.9 tokens/sec on 7B models). Qualitative cost efficiency is realized when fully utilizing the 100 Gbps network pipe alongside extensive memory capacity rather than raw compute cycles alone.

The r5n.24xlarge is suited for large-scale in-memory databases, distributed caching layers such as Redis, big data analytics clusters, and memory-intensive ETL pipelines that demand massive RAM capacities and high-throughput network connectivity across distributed cloud environments.
description: Amazon Web Services r5n.24xlarge is a memory-optimized, network-enhanced server powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores at 3.1 GHz, 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and a 100 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage. Benchmarks highlight high multi-core throughput (stress-ng multi-core score of 81,307.18), massive memory bandwidth (220.43 GB/sec read on 256 MB blocks), and strong Redis performance at 73.84 million SET operations per second. The r5n.24xlarge is well aligned with memory-heavy, network-intensive workloads, including large distributed in-memory databases, caching systems, and high-throughput data processing frameworks.
